import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

cases = {
    "int32": np.array([1, 2], dtype="i4"),
    "uint8": np.array([1, 2], dtype="u1"),
    "float32": np.array([1.5, 2.5], dtype="f4"),
    "string": np.array(["a", "b"], dtype="U2"),
    "datetime": np.array(["2020-01-01", "2020-01-02"], dtype="datetime64[ns]"),
}
for name, values in cases.items():
    ds = xr.Dataset(coords={"a": values})
    stacked = ds.stack(b=("a",))
    unstacked = stacked.unstack("b")
    print(name, values.dtype, stacked["a"].dtype, unstacked["a"].dtype,
          np.array_equal(stacked["a"].values, values),
          np.array_equal(unstacked["a"].values, values))

# Multiple levels with different dtypes.
ds = xr.Dataset(coords={
    "a": np.array([1, 2], dtype="i4"),
    "b": np.array([3, 4], dtype="u1"),
})
stacked = ds.stack(z=("a", "b"))
print("multi", stacked["a"].dtype, stacked["b"].dtype)
assert stacked["a"].dtype == np.dtype("i4")
assert stacked["b"].dtype == np.dtype("u1")

# Indexing a stacked level should preserve its dtype.

from xarray.core.indexing import PandasMultiIndexingAdapter
adapter = PandasMultiIndexingAdapter(stacked.indexes["z"], dtype=np.dtype("i4"), level="a")
print("explicit override", np.asarray(adapter, dtype=np.float32).dtype)
assert np.asarray(adapter, dtype=np.float32).dtype == np.float32

# Categorical MultiIndex levels remain materialized with category values.
